items.title: Bill Mays interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 5, 2025
items.q: And I’d never played with Lewis Nash and John Goldsby in a trio setting. I’d played with them in other groups. And I put them together for the date.

ctx.x: Yeah. There’s a learning curve to that and I’m sure that you mastered that a long time ago.

I remember, I did an album called “An Ellington Affair” for Concord records, all Duke and Billy Strayhorn tunes. And I’d never played with Lewis Nash and John Goldsby in a trio setting. I’d played with them in other groups. And I put them together for the date. We didn’t have a rehearsal, we just came into the studio, and man the recording is beautiful. And – ‘cause it was the right guys. They just locked it in from the minute we hit. And it was magic. So you know and I think it was magic because both those guys…
As you had all that experience.
